newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien declines comment on Clinton victory.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien declines comment on Clinton victory.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien on Wednesday refused to comment on U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election.
Chretien snubbed reporters on his way to a regular Liberal Party parliamentary caucus.
"No scrum," he said, referring to the usual practice of reporters' impromptu questioning of politicians outside the parliamentary chamber.
Later, his spokeswoman said that Chretien would not comment until the caucus was over.

"He doesn't have a comment right now. We don't have a comment until he'll scrum after (the Liberal) caucus, which is not going to be until noon (EST)." Chretien's spokeswoman Leslie Swartman told Reuters by phone.

Canada and the United States share the world's longest undefended border and are each other's largest trading partners. About $1 billion worth of goods crosses the border between the two countries each day.

Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on his way to the Liberal caucus that Clinton's re-election was no surprise and that it was time to get down to business in the relationship between the two countries now that the campaign was over.
"We have good relations with Mr. Clinton and now we can address some of the important problems that have been pending until the election was over," Axworthy said.
Asked whether the election results would have any impact on the controversial Helms-Burton law, which punishes foreign investors for doing business with Cuba, Axworthy said it was too early to say.

"We have to be realistic about the Helms-Burton (law). Mr. Helms remains and so does Mr. Burton. I think that maybe with the different composition of the U.S. Congress, there will be more dynamic for accommodation and compromise," Axworthy said.
Canada has adopted its own legislation in retaliation to the Helms-Burton law.
